trade_setups.asset: AMD Q2 AH — 5 PM ET August 4
trade_setups.thesis: AMD reports at the week's pivotal moment: the stock entered Tuesday at $484.64 (+12.7% Monday on PLTR read-through) and faces a 10% options-priced swing. PLTR confirmed the AI platform layer; AMD would confirm the GPU compute layer underneath. The AMD-Anthropic $5B MI450 deal raises the bar — the market expects Helios rack-scale commentary and MI450 deployment timelines alongside the revenue print. Confirming scenario: data-center above $7B with H1 2027 ramp confirmed. Breaking scenario: data-center at $5.5B or below, or material custom-silicon displacement commentary from AMZN Trainium or Google TPU at scale.
trade_setups.entry: Data-center above $7B and Helios ramp confirmed: $540+ opens as the next reference level from $484. Data-center $5.5B or below: $440–450 is the prior support zone.
trade_setups.invalidation: Data-center above $6.5B with in-line guidance but no Helios ramp specifics — the most ambiguous outcome at this entry level.

trade_setups.asset: WTI $79 — the last oil breach at the threshold
trade_setups.thesis: WTI touched $78.26 intraday — the first sub-$79 print since the Iran escalation began — before recovering to ~$80. The close determines whether the breach formally clears. A sustained Tuesday close below $79 reduces the regime breach count to 1-of-6 (30Y yield only). The supply-side dynamic (OPEC+ September 188k bpd increase, Iran ceasefire talks) continues to press prices lower. Iran denied the 'Hormuz deal' Trump cited, creating residual uncertainty. What reverses it: any IRGC military action or Trump escalation rhetoric restores both oil-side breaches simultaneously.
trade_setups.entry: Not a position; a regime threshold monitored at today's close. Two consecutive closes below $79 formally clear the oil-side breach.
trade_setups.invalidation: WTI close above $82 on a ceasefire reversal restores both oil-side breaches simultaneously.
trade_setups.horizon: Resolves at today's close; secondary check Friday NFP

trade_setups.asset: September hike binary — JOLTS through NFP sequence
trade_setups.thesis: September hike has declined from 82.4% (July 31) to approximately 55% Polymarket / 32% futures (August 4 AM), driven entirely by oil deflation. JOLTS June at 10 AM ET is the first intraday test. May JOLTS was 7.594M (highest since May 2024); above 7.8M signals continued labor tightness and can push September back toward 70%. ADP Wednesday and NFP Friday (consensus +91K) complete the sequence. The current level means oil deflation is dominating a backdrop that still includes ISM manufacturing at 55.6% with prices paid at 71.1%.
trade_setups.entry: Watch September hike probability in CME FedWatch within 30 minutes of each data release. JOLTS above 7.8M with September pushing back toward 65% is an early re-breach signal.
trade_setups.invalidation: JOLTS below 7.0M with September falling toward 45% clears the September hike risk as a regime concern; 30Y at 5.23% remains the primary breach regardless.
trade_setups.horizon: JOLTS 10 AM ET today; ADP Wednesday; NFP Friday August 7

bear_case: Iran denied the 'Hormuz deal' Trump cited publicly — the ceasefire framework is real but fragile, and a single IRGC military action restores both oil-side breaches in one session. ISM 55.6% with prices-paid at 71.1% is still the inflation backdrop; oil deflation is suppressing September hike probability, not labor or inflation improvement. PLTR at $144 premarket is approximately 85x forward sales — the 149% US commercial growth sets a quarterly sustainment bar above 100% YoY, and the stock re-rates materially on the first deceleration below 80%. AMD's +12.7% pre-earnings move means the AI thesis is fully priced ahead of a binary print; an in-line data-center result at $6B from $484 is a sell-the-news event in context. SPCX at 45%+ below its June IPO high has no near-term catalyst if Starlink profitability is not confirmed tonight. The read does not hold if SPX closes below 7,380 or if WTI closes back above $82.
